title: Data Structures
description: Overview of data structures in Python

dataList.data: Data structures are fundamental concepts in programming. Python provides built-in data structures like lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries, as well as more advanced structures in the collections module.
Built-in Data Structures
Lists: Ordered, mutable sequences
Tuples: Ordered, immutable sequences
Sets: Unordered collections of unique elements
Dictionaries: Key-value mappings
When to Use Each Structure
Choosing the right data structure can significantly impact your program's performance and readability.
Use lists when you need ordered, changeable collections
Use tuples for immutable sequences or when you need to return multiple values from a function
Use sets when you need unique elements and don't care about order
Use dictionaries for fast lookups by key
Advanced Data Structures
Python's collections module provides additional data structures:
deque: Double-ended queue for efficient appends and pops
Counter: For counting hashable objects
OrderedDict: Dictionary that remembers insertion order
defaultdict: Dictionary with default values
Time Complexity
Understanding the time complexity of operations on different data structures is crucial for writing efficient code.
List access: O(1), insertion/deletion: O(n)
Dictionary access: O(1) average case
Set operations: O(1) average case
Mastering data structures is essential for becoming a proficient Python programmer. Explore the specific sections for detailed implementations and use cases.
